weeks: What is real cannot be lost

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is restless, turbulent and stubborn. He says it feels as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees that it is difficult to control, but says that through practice and letting go, the mind can be steadied.
verse.for_you: Your mind is racing at 2am because it is trying to hold a future it cannot control. You do not have to win the night. Just let the messages wait and let your hands rest. The rating is not your life.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Ashtavakra lists the certainties that make the wise calm.
verse.sanskrit: चिन्तया जायते दुःखं नान्यथेहेति निश्चयी । तया हीनः सुखी शान्तः सर्वत्र गलितस्पृहः ॥
verse.line: Suffering is born of worry, nothing else. Free of worry, you are happy and at peace.
verse.translation: One who knows for certain that suffering here is born of worry and nothing else is free of it, happy, at peace, and unattached everywhere.
verse.why: Most suffering is made of worry; knowing what you can't control loosens it.
verse.misuse: Real problems still need attention; this is about the extra pain rumination adds.

prasang.title: The certainties of the calm
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra lists convictions that make a person calm: things arise and pass by nature, fortune and misfortune come in their time, and suffering is born of worry alone.
prasang.lesson: Most suffering is made of worry; knowing what you can't control loosens it.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka, who has stepped back from his throne to listen. He tells him that the only thing that creates suffering is worry. When you know that worry itself is the root of the pain, you can let it go. The things that happen in the world will keep happening, but the extra ache you carry is made by your own mind running ahead. That is where the trouble begins, and that is where you can begin to loosen it.
verse.for_you: You check work messages at 2am because your mind is trying to control a future it cannot see. The rating is not the problem. The worry that spins in the dark is what keeps you from sleeping. The rating only touches the work.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the field of battle, who is frozen by what might come. Krishna tells him to focus on the action itself, not on the fruit that will hang from it. Do your part with full attention, but do not let the outcome own you. The result is not in your hands. If you stop acting because you are afraid of the result, you will lose your footing before the fight even begins.
verse.for_you: You check those messages at two in the morning. That is your part. The rating is not yours to hold. Let the work go, and let your mind rest.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: ऐहिकः प्राक्तनं हन्ति प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनं बलात् । सर्वदा पुरुषस्पन्दस्तत्रानुद्वेगवाञ्जयी ॥
verse.line: Today's effort and yesterday's keep wrestling. Whoever stays calm through it wins.
verse.translation: Present effort overcomes the past, and the past can overpower the present. It is always a contest of human striving, and the one who stays calm wins.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Young Rama sits in the palace, feeling the weight of a kingdom he does not yet know how to rule. Vasishtha sits with him and says that the past is not a chain. It is simply the result of old effort. The future is not a locked door. It is the fruit of the work you do now. The two are always wrestling. The past pulls, and the present pushes. The one who stays calm in that contest wins. The mind that torments itself over what it cannot change is its own enemy.
verse.for_you: Your past effort brought you here, and today's effort is still shaping tomorrow. Let the contest go, and find your calm now.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna describes those whom he lifts out of the sea of mortality (12.7).
verse.sanskrit: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः । अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते ॥ तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् । भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् ॥
verse.line: Lay your work in me and keep your mind on me; I soon lift you out of the drowning sea.
verse.translation: But those who lay all their actions in me, intent on me, and worship me meditating with single-minded yoga — for them, whose minds are set on me, I soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth, Partha.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that there is a way out of the drowning sea of fear. It is not to stop working, but to lay your work in him and keep your mind on him. When you do this with single-minded focus, he becomes the one who lifts you. You do not have to carry the weight of the future alone.
verse.for_you: When the fear comes at two in the morning, try naming it. Then return your mind to your breath. You do not have to solve the future tonight. You only have to lay your work down and rest.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after he has lost his kingdom. She sees him giving up and tells him not to think less of himself or settle for little. She says to set his mind on what is truly good and stop fearing, and to pull himself together. Her point is that a past failure does not define who he is. The future is uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
verse.for_you: When that fear comes at 2am, name it as fear. Then let it sit and return your attention to your breath, and to what you can do tomorrow morning. The rating is not your life, and your breath is still yours.

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

script: It is 2am and your hands are on your phone again. The work messages are waiting. You are terrified that a single bad rating will unravel your visa and your family's life here. You feel like you are running on fumes, but your mind will not let the night rest.
Arjuna is in the middle of a battlefield. He has just heard Krishna's teachings about the self, but he is overwhelmed. He tells Krishna that the mind is restless and turbulent. Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

Krishna agrees with Arjuna. He says the mind is strong and stubborn. He says holding it is like holding the wind. But he does not say the mind is hopeless. He says practice and letting go can train it. This is easier said than done, because you cannot simply decide to stop thinking about the rating. The mind is trying to protect you by imagining every possible disaster. But the future is not yours to hold. The part of you that simply exists cannot be lost by a rating.

Tonight, let the messages wait. Put your phone down and let your hands rest. You do not have to win the night. The rating is not your life. Your life is the breath in your chest right now, and that is enough for this hour.
What if the wind is not your enemy, but only a thought passing through?

depth.life: You are lying awake at 2am, staring at the ceiling, your phone in your hand. The screen is dark but you are already checking the work messages, terrified that one bad rating will cost your visa and your family's life here.
depth.points: The mind is restless and strong, trying to hold a future that is not yours to control. What is real in you cannot be lost.
depth.practice: Place your phone face down on the table and turn away from the screen. Let your hands rest and let the messages wait.
depth.question: What is the one thing you cannot control tonight?
